name: Levetiracetam
summary: A broad-spectrum anticonvulsant acting at the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, notable for rapid onset, IV availability, and absence of CYP-mediated interactions.
mechanism: Binds synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A), modulating vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter release; exact anticonvulsant mechanism not fully defined.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Minimal hepatic metabolism (enzymatic hydrolysis); ~66% excreted unchanged in urine

dosing.adult: Start 250–500 mg BID; usual maintenance 1000–1500 mg BID; IV dose equals oral dose
dosing.renalAdjustment: Required — reduce dose when CrCl <80 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; not clearly teratogenic and appears relatively favorable among AEDs — do not stop abruptly in epilepsy
warnings: Behavioral/psychiatric effects — agitation, aggression, psychosis (more common in children)
Somnolence and asthenia — caution with driving
Class warning: suicidal thoughts and behavior
Rare serious skin reactions (DRESS/SJS) — stop for unexplained rash
safety.overdose: Somnolence, agitation, rarely respiratory depression; supportive care

clinicalPearls: Zero CYP interactions — the easiest AED to add to polypharmacy
Behavioral side effects (irritability, mood change) are common, especially in children, and are often the dose-limiting factor
good: A fast, well-tolerated add-on with no drug interactions — ideal in polypharmacy and acute settings (IV).
bad: Patients with psychiatric comorbidity — behavioral activation can be dose-limiting.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
